summary_out.changed: Removed every gate (loop-1/2 equity circuit breaker, loop-3 order-time book-imbalance filter) and replaced the algorithm with a zero-latency pass-through: on_order() submits every order — open and reduce-only alike — immediately in full, with no quote lookup, no state, and no deferral.
summary_out.outcome: pnl -50.3% vs base position-tier-gate (-8857.50 vs -5892.25), slippage 0.0% (both 0.0), sharpe -28.30; trade_count 152300, win_rate 0.327, max_drawdown -0.139%. is_weighted_bps 0.04497 vs base 0.04501 — essentially flat, did NOT fall toward simple's 0.039. FAILs vs the simple baseline (+156). All 12 train dates completed, per-date trade counts 449-28377 (no low-sample collapse).
summary_out.hypothesis: Acting on loop-3's directive to target implementation shortfall via order timing rather than skip gating: IS is measured against the arrival mid at decision time, so removing all execution friction (which delays fills and inflates IS) should drive is_weighted_bps down toward simple's 0.039 and restore P&L toward the base/simple envelope.
summary_out.next: The hypothesis was wrong and the result rules out a whole class of moves. (1) IS is fixed across binary submit/skip policies — loop-4's is_weighted_bps (0.04497) is within 0.08% of base; the base already submits non-skipped orders with zero deferral, so there is no latency to remove. simple's lower IS (0.039) comes from WHICH orders are in its fill set, not from when they fill. (2) Loop-4 reproduces loop-2's metrics to the digit (pnl -8857.50, sharpe -28.30, trade_count 152300) — both collapse to 'submit everything', the ungated upper bound on order flow, which loses the most because the sigma=200 per-trade edge is structurally negative. The submit/skip dichotomy is now exhausted in BOTH directions (gating loops 1-3, friction-removal loop 4). The only untried structural lever is order TRANSFORMATION: modify order quantity by slicing each parent into child orders, or add genuine timing offsets — not binary skip/submit. A future loop should test child-order slicing and measure its effect on is_weighted_bps and per-trade P&L.
